The mock balance tools were a proof of concept and were later removed in favor of real user-scoped tools; this issue records the transport foundation, not a current balance implementation.

**Evidence:** [monorepo/API scaffold](<https://github.com/ig-peralta/LazyFinance/commit/3e3de6f>), [initial MCP POC](<https://github.com/ig-peralta/LazyFinance/commit/a80905d>), [MCP library replacement](<https://github.com/ig-peralta/LazyFinance/commit/fed082a>).

**Product requirements:** [Linear document](<https://linear.app/lazyfinance/document/lazyfinance-product-requirements-document-f5e3f9499c0b>).

Title: Deliver an authenticated demo financial dashboard
Description:
**Delivered slice:** user-scoped API and server-rendered dashboard for account balances, recent activity, budgets and goals, month-to-date spending by tag, comparable previous-month spending, and spending-budget progress. Internal transfers are excluded from summary spending; income remains in API data but is not treated as available funds in the overview.

Functional foundation for testing the core; visual polish and goal-contribution semantics are later work.

**Evidence:** [merged implementation commit](<https://github.com/ig-peralta/LazyFinance/commit/295b379>).

**Product requirements:** [Linear document](<https://linear.app/lazyfinance/document/lazyfinance-product-requirements-document-f5e3f9499c0b>).

This records the first tool surface; MCP authorization for external clients (potentially OAuth) remains a Stage B decision.

Title: Define the core-first product requirements and validation gate
Description:
**Delivered slice:** set the product direction around a demo-backed financial core and explicit validation gate before Fintoc; define subsequent parallel tracks for financial API, UI, Firebase auth, MCP authorization, provider-neutral adapters and a first-party text agent, with voice later. Future financial actions remain possible even though the initial agent is read-only.

The requirements describe the intended development path, not a claim that Stage A or later stages have been completed.

Title: Review account balances, transfers, and transaction classification semantics
Description:
**Stage A - model review.** Use the seeded checking, savings and credit-card scenarios to decide how account balances, freshness, transfers, credit-card payments, income, and spending are represented. **Acceptance:** document the intended semantics and representative reconciliation examples; update model/calculations where needed; verify balances and user-scoped spending/comparisons remain consistent. Do not shape the core around Fintoc-specific payloads.

Title: Validate the financial-core model and record the Stage A gate decision
Description:
**Stage A exit gate.** Demonstrate realistic account, transaction, transfer, spending-budget and savings-goal scenarios with controlled data. Reconcile meanings of balances and movements, show consistent user-scoped API/dashboard/MCP results where applicable, and document nonblocking limitations.

**Done when:** any assumptions that would block provider ingestion are resolved; remaining questions are documented; there is an explicit decision that the model is good enough to begin Stage B parallel tracks, including the provider-neutral connector and eventual Fintoc adapter. This gate does not require polish or exhaustive analytics.

[Product requirements, Stage A exit criteria](<https://linear.app/lazyfinance/document/lazyfinance-product-requirements-document-f5e3f9499c0b>).

**Validation evidence:** record outcomes for [Stage A journeys J1-J4](<https://linear.app/lazyfinance/document/user-journeys-8320c2530763>) and their child stories before deciding the gate.

Title: As a user, understand what each account balance means
Description:
**Journey J1 - Account balances**

As a user with checking, savings and credit-card accounts, I want to see balances I can interpret per account so that I do not mistake card liability or recorded income for cash available to spend.

**Acceptance criteria**

* Each displayed balance identifies the account and type; the rules for checking, savings and credit-card balance meanings are documented with a representative demo reconciliation.
* The displayed amount and the underlying user-scoped API/MCP data agree for the same account, with any known freshness limitation or uncertainty explicit.
* Monthly recorded income alone is never used to state how much cash is currently available.
* A second user's account does not appear in the result.

**Validation:** demonstrate the examples in [J1 of the user journeys](<https://linear.app/lazyfinance/document/user-journeys-8320c2530763>). See also the [product requirements](<https://linear.app/lazyfinance/document/lazyfinance-product-requirements-document-f5e3f9499c0b>). This story supplies user-facing evidence for the parent model decision; it does not require UI polish.
Creator: ignacio.peralta.acev@gmail.com

Title: As a user, distinguish savings-goal progress from budget spending
Description:
**Journey J4 - Savings goal**

As a user with a savings target, I want any reported progress to reflect defined contributions so that I do not confuse a target or a spending-budget number with money saved.

**Acceptance criteria**

* Document with demo examples what counts as a contribution, how it relates to accounts and transfers, and how it differs from spending-budget progress.
* Display the goal target and, only when justified by that rule, a traceable contribution/progress amount. Otherwise show the target without an invented percentage.
* A tag or transfer by itself is not silently counted as a contribution unless the documented rule makes it one.
* Objective period/recurrence rules and the user-scoped read results remain consistent with those examples.

**Validation:** demonstrate [J4 of the user journeys](<https://linear.app/lazyfinance/document/user-journeys-8320c2530763>). Refer to the [product requirements](<https://linear.app/lazyfinance/document/lazyfinance-product-requirements-document-f5e3f9499c0b>).
Creator: ignacio.peralta.acev@gmail.com

Title: As a user, see spending without internal transfers counted as expenses
Description:
**Journey J2 - Actual spending**

As a user, I want monthly spending to represent purchases rather than money moved between my own accounts so that I can trust the total and compare periods.

**Acceptance criteria**

* A representative internal transfer and credit-card payment do not inflate spending or create new income; genuine purchases still count once in the overall spending total.
* The treatment is based on documented movement semantics, not an unexplained tag-name convention. Any classification exceptions are explicit.
* Overlapping tag amounts are not described as exclusive categories, and untagged spending does not disappear from the overall total.
* A partial current-month comparison uses a comparable prior period; totals and the comparison agree across user-scoped API/dashboard/MCP reads where exposed.

**Validation:** demonstrate transfer, payment, tagged and untagged examples from [J2 of the user journeys](<https://linear.app/lazyfinance/document/user-journeys-8320c2530763>). See the [product requirements](<https://linear.app/lazyfinance/document/lazyfinance-product-requirements-document-f5e3f9499c0b>).
Creator: ignacio.peralta.acev@gmail.com

Title: As a user, trace spending against my budget
Description:
**Journey J3 - Spending budget**

As a user with a grocery spending limit, I want to see what has been spent and what remains for its period so that I can understand whether I am within budget.

**Acceptance criteria**

* The budget's limit, spent, remaining and period are displayed or exposed consistently and can be traced to eligible user-owned transactions.
* An eligible movement bearing more than one relevant tag counts once within this budget; internal money movements do not consume the limit.
* Untagged spending is not silently presented as classified grocery spending, and the user can tell when category coverage is incomplete.
* At least one recurring-budget scenario is validated against representative demo movements; any missing classification/budget flow essential to trust this result is captured in the parent issue.

**Validation:** walk [J3 of the user journeys](<https://linear.app/lazyfinance/document/user-journeys-8320c2530763>) using the [product requirements](<https://linear.app/lazyfinance/document/lazyfinance-product-requirements-document-f5e3f9499c0b>) as scope. A scenario already supported by the dashboard still needs observable validation, not a duplicate implementation.
Creator: ignacio.peralta.acev@gmail.com
